observations: Photo 0: a bare inline 4 cylinder petrol car engine sitting on a wooden floor or bench in a workshop, out of the car.
Photo 0: silver engine cover with a Toyota oval emblem and red 'VVT-i' lettering; the smaller text on the cover is too low in resolution to read.
Photo 0: black plastic intake manifold, accessory pulleys and belt side visible; no gearbox attached.
Photo 0: the engine is dusty and grimy with dirt and oil residue around the block and manifold, consistent with a used pulled engine.
Photo 0: no engine code stamping, no plate and no label is readable.
Only one photo, taken with a phone (camera watermark 'CAMON 40') and a seller watermark; no running clip, no compression test, no close up of the block.

read_from: photo 0 engine cover emblem and 'VVT-i' lettering

risks.risk: Exact engine code and displacement unknown; Toyota VVT-i 4 cylinder engines of different sizes sell at different prices
risks.proof: A sharp close up of the engine code stamped on the block and of the full cover text
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced; the code sets the comparable

risks.risk: Engine does not run, burns oil or has low compression
risks.proof: A clip of the engine starting and idling on a test stand, or a compression gauge reading on each cylinder
risks.if_unproven: as a non running core engine

risks.risk: Cracked block or head, or a previously opened engine with a replaced head gasket
risks.proof: Close up photos of the head to block seam, both sides of the block and the oil under the filler cap

risks.risk: Missing or damaged accessories such as alternator, sensors, wiring or coils
risks.proof: Photos of all four sides of the engine showing what is attached
risks.if_unproven: as a long block without accessories

proof_requests: A sharp close up of the engine code stamped on the block (and the full text on the cover)
A clip of the engine running on a test stand
Photos of all four sides of the engine and the oil under the filler cap
Written terms of the 3 month guarantee
response.reason: The Toyota emblem and VVT-i lettering are readable but the engine code and displacement, which set the price, are not, so not even a worst case comparable can be chosen. A close up of the stamped engine code is needed before pricing it as a non running core.
